whyItExists.problem: A brand colour used in 50 places requires 50 edits to change. Without variables, CSS is repetitive and hard to maintain. Themes (dark/light mode) require duplicating entire rulesets.
whyItExists.solution: CSS custom properties (CSS variables) let you define a value once, reference it everywhere with var(), and change it in one place to update the entire design. Scoped to the cascade, they enable powerful theming.
whyItExists.whenToUse: Design tokens (colours, spacing, typography), theme switching (dark/light mode), component variants, dynamic values updated by JavaScript.
whyItExists.whenNotToUse: For values that never change or are used only once, a variable adds complexity without benefit.

explainModes.beginner: CSS variables are named values you define once and reuse everywhere. Change the variable once and every place that uses it updates automatically — like find-and-replace, but smarter.
explainModes.simple: Define: --variable-name: value on :root. Use: color: var(--variable-name). You can also provide a fallback: var(--brand, teal) uses teal if --brand is not set.
explainModes.standard: Custom properties cascade and inherit like any CSS property. They can be overridden in scoped selectors — set --color: blue on :root, then override with --color: red on .dark-theme. They are available in calc(), used in animations, and accessible from JavaScript.
explainModes.technical: Custom properties are live: JavaScript can write document.documentElement.style.setProperty('--accent', '#ff0000') and all elements using var(--accent) update immediately. They accept any valid CSS value (including strings — though strings cannot be used in calc()). They can hold complete property values including spaces and commas.
explainModes.deepDive: @property (Houdini CSS Properties and Values API) defines custom properties with a type, initial value, and inheritance flag. This enables animation between custom property values (normally not possible because the browser doesn't know the type) and syntax validation. @property --accent { syntax: '<color>'; initial-value: #4fd1c5; inherits: true; } makes --accent animatable with transition.

content.code:
<script>
// Toggle theme
document.documentElement.dataset.theme = 'light';

// Update a variable dynamically
window.addEventListener('scroll', () => {
  const progress = window.scrollY / (document.body.offsetHeight - window.innerHeight);
  document.documentElement.style.setProperty('--scroll-progress', progress);
});
</script>

questions.question: How do you define a CSS custom property (variable)?
questions.explanation: CSS custom properties start with double dashes: --accent: #4fd1c5. They are typically defined on :root to make them globally available.

questions.question: CSS variables can be updated with JavaScript to create dynamic styles.
questions.explanation: JavaScript can read and write CSS variables using getPropertyValue and setProperty on element.style or document.documentElement.style. This enables dynamic theming, scroll-driven animations, and interactive styling without re-applying CSS classes.

faq.q: What is the difference between CSS variables and SASS/LESS variables?
faq.a: SASS/LESS variables are compiled away — they exist only in source code and produce static CSS. CSS custom properties are live in the browser — they can be changed by JavaScript, they cascade and inherit, and they can be inspected in DevTools.

faq.q: Can I use CSS variables in media queries?
faq.a: Not directly in the @media condition itself (you can't write @media (min-width: var(--breakpoint))). But you can override variable values inside media queries: @media (prefers-color-scheme: light) { :root { --bg: white; } }.
